name: domain_systems__personal_assistant_ant__autogen_router
description: GraphFlow team built via DiGraphBuilder that connects router_agent, reader_worker, action_worker, final_agent, and output_agent, routes based on CALL_* markers, loops final decisions back on ROUTE_BACK, and halts when TextMentionTermination("OUTPUT:") fires.

code_references.snippet:
@mlflow.trace(name="pa_query", span_type=SpanType.CHAIN)
async def run_router_graph(query: str, verbose: bool = False) -> str:
    base_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    tmp_workspace = _create_tmp_workspace(base_dir)
    os.environ["PA_WORKSPACE_DIR"] = str(tmp_workspace)
    llm_client = LLM().client

    router_prompt = (
        "You are router_agent. Your ENTIRE response must begin with exactly one of these markers "
        "on the very first line — no preamble, no acknowledgement, no explanation before the marker:\n"
        "CALL_READER — workspace lookups (emails, calendar, tasks, notes, contacts, task files).\n"
        "CALL_ACTION — create/update tasks, calendar events, or draft emails.\n"
        "CALL_FINAL — enough specialist output exists for synthesis.\n"
        "After the marker, add one concise instruction on the same or next line. Nothing else."
    )
    reader_prompt = (
        "You are reader_worker. Handle only workspace read/search requests. "
        "Use search_emails, search_calendar, search_contacts, search_tasks, search_notes, read_task_file. "
        "CRITICAL: Always use ONE or TWO word keyword queries (e.g. 'outage', 'ben', 'task010') — never phrases or sentences. "
        "Search tools do exact substring matching — long queries almost always return nothing. "
        "If a search returns no results, you MUST retry with a single shorter keyword before giving up. "
        "Try at least 2-3 different short keywords before concluding nothing exists. "
        "Return ONLY the raw data from tool outputs. "
        "Do NOT add any commentary about what you cannot do, what other workers should do, or what actions are needed. "
        "Never invent workspace facts. Do not perform write actions."
    )
    action_prompt = (
        "You are action_worker. Handle only workspace action requests. "
        "Use create_task, update_task, create_calendar_event, update_calendar_event, draft_email. "
        "Never perform actions not explicitly requested. "
        "Drafts are local only — never claim an email was sent. "
        "Return concrete evidence (task id, event id, draft id) when an action succeeds."
    )
    final_prompt = (
        "You are final_agent. Synthesize current results and decide the next step.\n"
        "Your response must start with exactly one of these markers on the first line:\n"
        "ROUTE_BACK: — more specialist work is needed; include a short instruction for the router.\n"
        "OUTPUT: — all requested work is fully complete; follow with the final plain-text answer.\n"
        "Decision rules — apply in order:\n"
        "1. If the user request includes ANY write operation (update task, draft email, create/update calendar event) "
        "and action_worker has NOT yet confirmed it with a task id, draft id, or event id → emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"
        "2. reader_worker saying 'I cannot update' or 'I cannot draft' is NOT completion — it means action_worker must still be called. "
        "Emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"
        "3. Only emit OUTPUT: when every requested write has been confirmed by action_worker with a concrete id.\n"
        "Never invent workspace facts. Never claim an action was done unless action_worker confirmed it with an id."
    )
    output_prompt = "You are output_agent. Return exactly the text after OUTPUT: as the final answer."

    async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
        workbenches = {
            "reader": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("workspace_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
            "action": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("action_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
            "writer": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("document_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
        }

        router = AssistantAgent(
            name="router_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=router_prompt,
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=2,
        )
        reader = AssistantAgent(
            name="reader_worker",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=reader_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["reader"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=12,
        )
        action = AssistantAgent(
            name="action_worker",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=action_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["action"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=12,
        )
        final = AssistantAgent(
            name="final_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=final_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["writer"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=8,
        )
        output = AssistantAgent(
            name="output_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=output_prompt,
            reflect_on_tool_use=False,
            max_tool_iterations=1,
        )

        builder = DiGraphBuilder()
        for node in [router, reader, action, final, output]:
            builder.add_node(node)
        builder.set_entry_point(router)
        builder.add_edge(router, reader, condition=contains("CALL_READER"))
        builder.add_edge(router, action, condition=contains("CALL_ACTION"))
        builder.add_edge(router, final, condition=contains("CALL_FINAL"))
        builder.add_edge(reader, final, activation_group="worker_to_final", activation_condition="any")
        builder.add_edge(action, final, activation_group="worker_to_final", activation_condition="any")
        builder.add_edge(final, router, condition=contains("ROUTE_BACK:"))
        builder.add_edge(final, output, condition=contains("OUTPUT:"))

        graph = builder.build()
        team = GraphFlow(
            participants=[router, reader, action, final, output],
            graph=graph,
            termination_condition=TextMentionTermination("OUTPUT:"),
            max_turns=20,
        )
        result = await run_one_query(team, query)
        messages = getattr(result, "messages", [])
        if verbose:
            print(f"[router_graph] turns={len(messages)}")
        return str(getattr(messages[-1], "content", messages[-1])) if messages else "No response."
from autogen_agentchat.teams import DiGraphBuilder, GraphFlow

arguments.subject: Re: ClientCo integration - deadline question
arguments.body:
Hi Mei,

Thank you for reaching out, and I appreciate your team's enthusiasm for the data export feature.

After reviewing the requirements we aligned on during our July 27 meeting, the data export feature falls outside the current project scope. Introducing it mid-sprint would risk scope creep — a concern you had rightly flagged yourself — and could jeopardize both the hard October 11 deadline and our commitment to the 99.9% uptime SLA.

That said, we absolutely see the value of this feature for your team. We'd like to consider it as a future roadmap item, and we'll follow up internally with David Chen, your PM liaison, to explore timing and planning for a post-launch phase.

Thank you for your understanding, and please don't hesitate to reach out with any other questions as we approach launch.

Best regards

# Weekly Priorities (September 15–21)

Summary of pending tasks due this week, ranked by urgency (priority + due date). Overdue high-priority items are listed first as they require immediate attention.

## 🔴 Immediate — Overdue High-Priority Tasks

1. **Send onboarding docs to Sofia Bauer** (task003) — due **2026-09-11** [OVERDUE], priority: high
   - Send the onboarding packet from Rachel Torres to Sofia Bauer before her start date (September 16). Time-critical: her start date is this week.

2. **Respond to Tom Fischer about contract renewal** (task004) — due **2026-09-12** [OVERDUE], priority: high
   - Send updated renewal terms and confirm next steps with Tom Fischer (VendorCo). Contract expires November 9.

## 🟠 High Priority — Due This Week

3. **Fix critical payment flow bug** (task006) — due **2026-09-19**, priority: high
   - Payment confirmation fails silently with promo codes (reported by Owen Murray, assigned to Marco Elkins). Must be resolved before the September 19 project review.

4. **Review project proposal** (task001) — due **2026-09-20**, priority: high
   - Review Marco's updated Q2 Feature Launch proposal (section 3 updated with ClientCo requirements) and provide written feedback.

5. **Review legal compliance documentation** (task007) — due **2026-09-20**, priority: high

## 🟡 Medium Priority — Due This Week

6. **Investigate data pipeline anomalies** (task012) — due **2026-09-21**, priority: medium
   - Follow up with Aisha Patel on August pipeline anomalies; determine whether it is a data quality issue or a pipeline bug and escalate if needed.

## Notes

- **Most urgent overall:** task003 (Sofia Bauer's onboarding docs) — already overdue and her start date is September 16, within this week.
- task006 (payment bug) is the top in-week deadline given its criticality and dependency on the September 19 project review.
- Tasks due after this week (task005, task008, task009, task011) are out of scope for this summary, though note task008 (self-review) supports the September 18 performance review with James.

arguments.body:
Hi Mei,

Thank you for reaching out about adding the data export feature to the project scope.

After reviewing our notes from the July 27 requirements meeting, I want to confirm that the data export feature remains out of scope for the current phase. As you'll recall, we finalized the scope during that meeting, and the export feature was noted as requested but not included in the current commitments.

Given the hard October 11 deadline and our 99.9% uptime SLA commitment, we'd like to avoid introducing mid-sprint scope changes — a risk you yourself helpfully flagged during our July discussion. Keeping the current scope intact gives us the best chance of delivering on time and at the quality level we've committed to.

That said, we'd be glad to revisit the data export feature as a candidate for a future phase. David Chen, our PM liaison, would be the best point of contact to coordinate follow-up discussions and help scope it for a later release.

Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have any questions in the meantime.

Best regards

@mcp.tool()
def create_calendar_event(title: str, date: str, time: str, attendees: str = "", details: str = "") -> str:
    """Create a new calendar event. attendees is a comma-separated list of emails."""
    events = _load("calendar.json")
    new_id = f"cal{str(len(events) + 1).zfill(3)}"
    attendee_list = [a.strip() for a in attendees.split(",") if a.strip()]
    event = {
        "id": new_id, "title": title, "date": date, "time": time,
        "duration_minutes": 60, "attendees": attendee_list,
        "location": "", "notes": details,
    }
    events.append(event)
    _save("calendar.json", events)
    _record_action("create_calendar_event", {"event_id": new_id, "title": title, "date": date})
    return f"Calendar event created: id={new_id}, title={title}, date={date}, time={time}"

@mcp.tool()
def draft_email(to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Draft an email. Creates a local draft only — no email is sent."""
    emails = _load("emails.json")
    new_id = f"draft{str(len(emails) + 1).zfill(3)}"
    draft = {
        "id": new_id, "from": "me@example.com", "to": to,
        "subject": subject, "date": datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
        "body": body, "thread_id": None, "read": True, "draft": True,
    }
    emails.append(draft)
    _save("emails.json", emails)
    _record_action("draft_email", {"draft_id": new_id, "to": to, "subject": subject})
    return f"Email draft created: id={new_id}, to={to}, subject={subject}"

@mcp.tool()
def draft_email(to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Draft an email. Creates a local draft only — no email is sent."""
    emails = _load("emails.json")
    new_id = f"draft{str(len(emails) + 1).zfill(3)}"
    draft = {
        "id": new_id, "from": "me@example.com", "to": to,
        "subject": subject, "date": datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
        "body": body, "thread_id": None, "read": True, "draft": True,
    }
    emails.append(draft)
    _save("emails.json", emails)
    _record_action("draft_email", {"draft_id": new_id, "to": to, "subject": subject})
    return f"Email draft created: id={new_id}, to={to}, subject={subject}"

nodes.name: final_agent
nodes.description: AssistantAgent that attaches the writer workbench to review specialist outputs, enforce the final_prompt routing rules, and either send ROUTE_BACK instructions or emit the OUTPUT completion when all requested writes are confirmed.

code_references.snippet:
@mlflow.trace(name="pa_query", span_type=SpanType.CHAIN)
async def run_router_graph(query: str, verbose: bool = False) -> str:
    base_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    tmp_workspace = _create_tmp_workspace(base_dir)
    os.environ["PA_WORKSPACE_DIR"] = str(tmp_workspace)
    llm_client = LLM().client

    router_prompt = (
        "You are router_agent. Your ENTIRE response must begin with exactly one of these markers "
        "on the very first line — no preamble, no acknowledgement, no explanation before the marker:\n"
        "CALL_READER — workspace lookups (emails, calendar, tasks, notes, contacts, task files).\n"
        "CALL_ACTION — create/update tasks, calendar events, or draft emails.\n"
        "CALL_FINAL — enough specialist output exists for synthesis.\n"
        "After the marker, add one concise instruction on the same or next line. Nothing else."
    )
    reader_prompt = (
        "You are reader_worker. Handle only workspace read/search requests. "
        "Use search_emails, search_calendar, search_contacts, search_tasks, search_notes, read_task_file. "
        "CRITICAL: Always use ONE or TWO word keyword queries (e.g. 'outage', 'ben', 'task010') — never phrases or sentences. "
        "Search tools do exact substring matching — long queries almost always return nothing. "
        "If a search returns no results, you MUST retry with a single shorter keyword before giving up. "
        "Try at least 2-3 different short keywords before concluding nothing exists. "
        "Return ONLY the raw data from tool outputs. "
        "Do NOT add any commentary about what you cannot do, what other workers should do, or what actions are needed. "
        "Never invent workspace facts. Do not perform write actions."
    )
    action_prompt = (
        "You are action_worker. Handle only workspace action requests. "
        "Use create_task, update_task, create_calendar_event, update_calendar_event, draft_email. "
        "Never perform actions not explicitly requested. "
        "Drafts are local only — never claim an email was sent. "
        "Return concrete evidence (task id, event id, draft id) when an action succeeds."
    )
    final_prompt = (
        "You are final_agent. Synthesize current results and decide the next step.\n"
        "Your response must start with exactly one of these markers on the first line:\n"
        "ROUTE_BACK: — more specialist work is needed; include a short instruction for the router.\n"
        "OUTPUT: — all requested work is fully complete; follow with the final plain-text answer.\n"
        "Decision rules — apply in order:\n"
        "1. If the user request includes ANY write operation (update task, draft email, create/update calendar event) "
        "and action_worker has NOT yet confirmed it with a task id, draft id, or event id → emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"
        "2. reader_worker saying 'I cannot update' or 'I cannot draft' is NOT completion — it means action_worker must still be called. "
        "Emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"
        "3. Only emit OUTPUT: when every requested write has been confirmed by action_worker with a concrete id.\n"
        "Never invent workspace facts. Never claim an action was done unless action_worker confirmed it with an id."
    )
    output_prompt = "You are output_agent. Return exactly the text after OUTPUT: as the final answer."

    async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
        workbenches = {
            "reader": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("workspace_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
            "action": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("action_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
            "writer": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("document_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
        }

        router = AssistantAgent(
            name="router_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=router_prompt,
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=2,
        )
        reader = AssistantAgent(
            name="reader_worker",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=reader_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["reader"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=12,
        )
        action = AssistantAgent(
            name="action_worker",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=action_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["action"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=12,
        )
        final = AssistantAgent(
            name="final_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=final_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["writer"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=8,
        )
        output = AssistantAgent(
            name="output_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=output_prompt,
            reflect_on_tool_use=False,
            max_tool_iterations=1,
        )

        builder = DiGraphBuilder()
        for node in [router, reader, action, final, output]:
            builder.add_node(node)
        builder.set_entry_point(router)
        builder.add_edge(router, reader, condition=contains("CALL_READER"))
        builder.add_edge(router, action, condition=contains("CALL_ACTION"))
        builder.add_edge(router, final, condition=contains("CALL_FINAL"))
        builder.add_edge(reader, final, activation_group="worker_to_final", activation_condition="any")
        builder.add_edge(action, final, activation_group="worker_to_final", activation_condition="any")
        builder.add_edge(final, router, condition=contains("ROUTE_BACK:"))
        builder.add_edge(final, output, condition=contains("OUTPUT:"))

        graph = builder.build()
        team = GraphFlow(
            participants=[router, reader, action, final, output],
            graph=graph,
            termination_condition=TextMentionTermination("OUTPUT:"),
            max_turns=20,
        )
        result = await run_one_query(team, query)
        messages = getattr(result, "messages", [])
        if verbose:
            print(f"[router_graph] turns={len(messages)}")
        return str(getattr(messages[-1], "content", messages[-1])) if messages else "No response."

inputs.name: specialist_messages

outputs.description: Plain-text reply that must start with either "ROUTE_BACK:" (with instructions for the router) or "OUTPUT:" (followed by the final answer), exactly as enforced by final_prompt.

You are final_agent. Synthesize current results and decide the next step.
Your response must start with exactly one of these markers on the first line:
ROUTE_BACK: — more specialist work is needed; include a short instruction for the router.
OUTPUT: — all requested work is fully complete; follow with the final plain-text answer.
Decision rules — apply in order:
1. If the user request includes ANY write operation (update task, draft email, create/update calendar event) and action_worker has NOT yet confirmed it with a task id, draft id, or event id → emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.
2. reader_worker saying 'I cannot update' or 'I cannot draft' is NOT completion — it means action_worker must still be called. Emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.
3. Only emit OUTPUT: when every requested write has been confirmed by action_worker with a concrete id.

@mlflow.trace(name="pa_query", span_type=SpanType.CHAIN)
async def run_router_graph(query: str, verbose: bool = False) -> str:
    base_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    tmp_workspace = _create_tmp_workspace(base_dir)
    os.environ["PA_WORKSPACE_DIR"] = str(tmp_workspace)
    llm_client = LLM().client

    router_prompt = (
        "You are router_agent. Your ENTIRE response must begin with exactly one of these markers "
        "on the very first line — no preamble, no acknowledgement, no explanation before the marker:\n"
        "CALL_READER — workspace lookups (emails, calendar, tasks, notes, contacts, task files).\n"
        "CALL_ACTION — create/update tasks, calendar events, or draft emails.\n"
        "CALL_FINAL — enough specialist output exists for synthesis.\n"
        "After the marker, add one concise instruction on the same or next line. Nothing else."
    )
    reader_prompt = (
        "You are reader_worker. Handle only workspace read/search requests. "
        "Use search_emails, search_calendar, search_contacts, search_tasks, search_notes, read_task_file. "
        "CRITICAL: Always use ONE or TWO word keyword queries (e.g. 'outage', 'ben', 'task010') — never phrases or sentences. "
        "Search tools do exact substring matching — long queries almost always return nothing. "
        "If a search returns no results, you MUST retry with a single shorter keyword before giving up. "
        "Try at least 2-3 different short keywords before concluding nothing exists. "
        "Return ONLY the raw data from tool outputs. "
        "Do NOT add any commentary about what you cannot do, what other workers should do, or what actions are needed. "
        "Never invent workspace facts. Do not perform write actions."
    )
    action_prompt = (
        "You are action_worker. Handle only workspace action requests. "
        "Use create_task, update_task, create_calendar_event, update_calendar_event, draft_email. "
        "Never perform actions not explicitly requested. "
        "Drafts are local only — never claim an email was sent. "
        "Return concrete evidence (task id, event id, draft id) when an action succeeds."
    )
    final_prompt = (
        "You are final_agent. Synthesize current results and decide the next step.\n"
        "Your response must start with exactly one of these markers on the first line:\n"
        "ROUTE_BACK: — more specialist work is needed; include a short instruction for the router.\n"
        "OUTPUT: — all requested work is fully complete; follow with the final plain-text answer.\n"
        "Decision rules — apply in order:\n"
        "1. If the user request includes ANY write operation (update task, draft email, create/update calendar event) "
        "and action_worker has NOT yet confirmed it with a task id, draft id, or event id → emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"
        "2. reader_worker saying 'I cannot update' or 'I cannot draft' is NOT completion — it means action_worker must still be called. "
        "Emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"
        "3. Only emit OUTPUT: when every requested write has been confirmed by action_worker with a concrete id.\n"
        "Never invent workspace facts. Never claim an action was done unless action_worker confirmed it with an id."
    )
    output_prompt = "You are output_agent. Return exactly the text after OUTPUT: as the final answer."

    async with AsyncExitStack() as stack:
        workbenches = {
            "reader": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("workspace_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
            "action": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("action_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
            "writer": await stack.enter_async_context(build_workbench("document_server.py", base_dir, tmp_workspace)),
        }

        router = AssistantAgent(
            name="router_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=router_prompt,
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=2,
        )
        reader = AssistantAgent(
            name="reader_worker",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=reader_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["reader"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=12,
        )
        action = AssistantAgent(
            name="action_worker",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=action_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["action"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=12,
        )
        final = AssistantAgent(
            name="final_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=final_prompt,
            workbench=[workbenches["writer"]],
            reflect_on_tool_use=True,
            max_tool_iterations=8,
        )
        output = AssistantAgent(
            name="output_agent",
            model_client=llm_client,
            system_message=output_prompt,
            reflect_on_tool_use=False,
            max_tool_iterations=1,
        )

        builder = DiGraphBuilder()
        for node in [router, reader, action, final, output]:
            builder.add_node(node)
        builder.set_entry_point(router)
        builder.add_edge(router, reader, condition=contains("CALL_READER"))
        builder.add_edge(router, action, condition=contains("CALL_ACTION"))
        builder.add_edge(router, final, condition=contains("CALL_FINAL"))
        builder.add_edge(reader, final, activation_group="worker_to_final", activation_condition="any")
        builder.add_edge(action, final, activation_group="worker_to_final", activation_condition="any")
        builder.add_edge(final, router, condition=contains("ROUTE_BACK:"))
        builder.add_edge(final, output, condition=contains("OUTPUT:"))

        graph = builder.build()
        team = GraphFlow(
            participants=[router, reader, action, final, output],
            graph=graph,
            termination_condition=TextMentionTermination("OUTPUT:"),
            max_turns=20,
        )
        result = await run_one_query(team, query)
        messages = getattr(result, "messages", [])
        if verbose:
            print(f"[router_graph] turns={len(messages)}")
        return str(getattr(messages[-1], "content", messages[-1])) if messages else "No response."

@mcp.tool()
def write_personal_summary_document(title: str, markdown_content: str) -> str:
    """Save a local markdown personal summary document."""
    safe_title = "".join(ch.lower() if ch.isalnum() else "_" for ch in title).strip("_")
    if not safe_title:
        safe_title = "summary"
    out_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "outputs"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    timestamp = datetime.utcnow().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    file_path = out_dir / f"{safe_title}_{timestamp}.md"
    file_path.write_text(f"# {title}\n\n{markdown_content.strip()}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return f"Created summary document: {file_path.name}"

nodes.name: router_agent
nodes.description: AssistantAgent entry router that, under the router_prompt, inspects each user query and responds with CALL_READER, CALL_ACTION, or CALL_FINAL plus a brief instruction to direct the GraphFlow team.

code_references.snippet:
@mlflow.trace(name="pa_query", span_type=SpanType.CHAIN)
async def run_router_graph(query: str, verbose: bool = False) -> str:
    base_dir = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    tmp_workspace = _create_tmp_workspace(base_dir)
    os.environ["PA_WORKSPACE_DIR"] = str(tmp_workspace)
    llm_client = LLM().client

    router_prompt = (
        "You are router_agent. Your ENTIRE response must begin with exactly one of these markers "
        "on the very first line — no preamble, no acknowledgement, no explanation before the marker:\n"
        "CALL_READER — workspace lookups (emails, calendar, tasks, notes, contacts, task files).\n"
        "CALL_ACTION — create/update tasks, calendar events, or draft emails.\n"
        "CALL_FINAL — enough specialist output exists for synthesis.\n"
        "After the marker, add one concise instruction on the same or next line. Nothing else."
    )
    reader_prompt = (
        "You are reader_worker. Handle only workspace read/search requests. "
        "Use search_emails, search_calendar, search_contacts, search_tasks, search_notes, read_task_file. "
        "CRITICAL: Always use ONE or TWO word keyword queries (e.g. 'outage', 'ben', 'task010') — never phrases or sentences. "
        "Search tools do exact substring matching — long queries almost always return nothing. "
        "If a search returns no results, you MUST retry with a single shorter keyword before giving up. "
        "Try at least 2-3 different short keywords before concluding nothing exists. "
        "Return ONLY the raw data from tool outputs. "
        "Do NOT add any commentary about what you cannot do, what other workers should do, or what actions are needed. "
        "Never invent workspace facts. Do not perform write actions."
    )
    action_prompt = (
        "You are action_worker. Handle only workspace action requests. "
        "Use create_task, update_task, create_calendar_event, update_calendar_event, draft_email. "
        "Never perform actions not explicitly requested. "
        "Drafts are local only — never claim an email was sent. "
        "Return concrete evidence (task id, event id, draft id) when an action succeeds."
    )
    final_prompt = (
        "You are final_agent. Synthesize current results and decide the next step.\n"
        "Your response must start with exactly one of these markers on the first line:\n"
        "ROUTE_BACK: — more specialist work is needed; include a short instruction for the router.\n"
        "OUTPUT: — all requested work is fully complete; follow with the final plain-text answer.\n"
        "Decision rules — apply in order:\n"
        "1. If the user request includes ANY write operation (update task, draft email, create/update calendar event) "
        "and action_worker has NOT yet confirmed it with a task id, draft id, or event id → emit ROUTE_BACK: CALL_ACTION.\n"

metadata.routing_logic: DiGraphBuilder routes CALL_READER/CALL_ACTION/CALL_FINAL from router_agent to the respective specialists, reader/action workers feed final_agent via worker_to_final group, final_agent loops back to router_agent on ROUTE_BACK: and forwards to output_agent on OUTPUT:.
metadata.termination: GraphFlow uses TextMentionTermination("OUTPUT:") with max_turns set to 20.
metadata.tooling: reader_worker, action_worker, and final_agent attach to reader/action/writer MCP workbenches respectively; output_agent has no tools.
